questions.prompt: After the victory the general gave rewards to the brave soldiers.
questions.answer: Post victōriam imperātor mīlitibus fortibus praemia dedit.

questions.prompt: The poet showed his new verses to the king.
questions.answer: Poēta rēgī nova carmina ostendit.

questions.prompt: We entrusted the letters to a faithful messenger.
questions.answer: Epistulās fidēlī nūntiō crēdidimus.

questions.prompt: The mother prepared a feast for her returning sons.
questions.answer: Māter fīliīs redeuntibus epulās parāvit.

questions.prompt: You cannot persuade the stubborn old man with words.
questions.answer: Verbīs pertinācī senī persuādēre nōn potes.

questions.prompt: The gods above favor those who dare reckless deeds.
questions.answer: Superī eīs favent quī facta temerāria audent.

questions.prompt: Excessive wine harms both the body and the mind.
questions.answer: Vīnum nimium et corporī et animō nocet.

questions.prompt: The wise king had great authority among the people.
questions.answer: Rēgī sapientī magna auctōritās in populō erat.

questions.prompt: I have no hope of safety left.
questions.answer: Mihi nūlla spēs salūtis reliqua est.

questions.prompt: The bold maiden had a heart full of courage.
questions.answer: Virginī audācī cor plēnum virtūtis erat.

questions.prompt: We have many friends, but few true ones.
questions.answer: Nōbīs multī amīcī sed paucī vērī sunt.

questions.prompt: For a brave man death is not to be feared.
questions.answer: Virō fortī mors nōn timenda est.

questions.prompt: The waters of the deep pool seemed calm to the sailors.
questions.answer: Nautīs aquae stāgnī altī placidae vidēbantur.

questions.prompt: The victory brought glory to the whole city.
questions.answer: Victōria tōtī urbī glōriam attulit.

questions.prompt: The cavalry served as a protection for the fleeing troops.
questions.answer: Equitēs fugientibus cōpiīs praesidiō erant.

questions.prompt: This news was a great joy to all the citizens.
questions.answer: Hic nūntius omnibus cīvibus magnae laetitiae fuit.

questions.prompt: The bridge's collapse was a ruin to the enemy.
questions.answer: Pontis ruīna hostibus exitiō fuit.

questions.prompt: Your courage will be an example to future generations.
questions.answer: Virtūs tua futūrīs generibus exemplō erit.

questions.prompt: When the city had been captured, the leader granted freedom to the prisoners.
questions.answer: Urbe captā dux captīvīs lībertātem dedit.

questions.prompt: Fortune often denies success to the reckless.
questions.answer: Fors saepe temerāriīs successum negat.

questions.prompt: The teacher explained the difficult truth to his eager students.
questions.answer: Magister studiōsīs discipulīs difficilem vēritātem exposuit.

questions.prompt: The senators refused to yield to the arrogant tyrant.
questions.answer: Senātōrēs superbō tyrannō cēdere nōluērunt.

questions.prompt: The general showed the captured standards to the grieving citizens.
questions.answer: Dux cīvibus lūgentibus signa capta ostendit.

questions.prompt: The teacher gave difficult books to the hard-working students.
questions.answer: Grammaticus discipulīs labōriōsīs librōs difficilēs dedit.

questions.prompt: The merchant entrusted his riches to a faithful friend.
questions.answer: Mercātor dīvitiās suās amīcō fidēlī crēdidit.

questions.prompt: The mother handed a secret sign to her daughter.
questions.answer: Māter fīliae signum arcānum trādidit.

questions.prompt: We could not persuade the unwilling king to spare the captives.
questions.answer: Rēgī invītō persuādēre nōn potuimus ut captīvīs parceret.

questions.prompt: The armed enemy harmed the sleeping farmers.
questions.answer: Hostēs armātī agricolīs dormientibus nocuērunt.

questions.prompt: The general ordered the weary legions to return home.
questions.answer: Dux legiōnibus fessīs imperāvit ut domum redīrent.

questions.prompt: The poor old man had neither money nor friends.
questions.answer: Senī pauperī nec pecūnia nec amīcī erant.

questions.prompt: The brave maiden had a great name among the people.
questions.answer: Fortī virginī magnum nōmen in populō erat.

questions.prompt: We have many books but little leisure.
questions.answer: Nōbīs multī librī sed parvum ōtium est.

questions.prompt: The soldiers built a bridge for the advancing army.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs exercituī prōgredientī pontem aedificāvērunt.

questions.prompt: For me these threats mean nothing.
questions.answer: Mihi hae minae nihil significant.

questions.prompt: The mother prepared a modest meal for her hungry children.
questions.answer: Māter līberīs ēsurientibus cēnam modicam parāvit.

questions.prompt: To the weary traveler the shade of the tree was pleasing.
questions.answer: Fessō viātōrī umbra arboris grāta erat.

questions.prompt: The consul granted citizenship to the loyal allies.
questions.answer: Cōnsul sociīs fidēlibus cīvitātem dedit.

questions.prompt: The gods granted a long life to the pious king.
questions.answer: Dī rēgī piō longam vītam dedērunt.

questions.prompt: You have a great opportunity, if only you seize it.
questions.answer: Tibi magna occāsiō est, sī modo eam rapis.

questions.prompt: The senate decreed a triumph for the victorious commander.
questions.answer: Senātus imperātōrī victōrī triumphum dēcrēvit.

questions.prompt: Fortune often favors those who dare.
questions.answer: Fortūna saepe audentibus favet.

questions.prompt: The physician gave the sick woman a bitter remedy.
questions.answer: Medicus aegrae fēminae remedium amārum dedit.

questions.prompt: For the grieving widow there was no hope of consolation.
questions.answer: Lūgentī viduae nūlla spēs sōlāciī erat.
